### Bug Scenario and Root Cause

The issue involves the handling of the multiplication operator `(*)` in F# syntax highlighting. The Prism highlighter mistakenly interprets `(*)` as the start of a multi-line comment (`(* ... *)`), because it recognizes the pattern as a comment instead of an operator. This incorrect identification causes the page to highlight code erroneously, as seen in the provided screenshot.

### Bug Location and Analysis

The issue is located in the F# language definition file `components/prism-fsharp.js`. The problematic part resides in the regex pattern that defines the handling of comments:

```javascript
pattern: /(^|[^\\])\(\*[\s\S]*?\*\)/
```

This regex pattern matches anything that starts with `(*`, treating it as a comment block, without considering that `(*)` could be used as a valid operator function in F#.

### Patch

To resolve this, we'll update the regex pattern to exclude cases where `(*)` is used as an expression rather than a comment. We will refine the comment pattern to check that it does not end with `)` immediately after `*`.

```javascript
### components/prism-fsharp.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
\t\t\tpattern: /(^|[^\\\\])\\(\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\)/,
=======
\t\t\tpattern: /(^|[^\\\\])\\(\\*[^)]?[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\)/,
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

This alteration in the regex pattern prevents misinterpretation of the `(*)` operator as a comment, allowing the highlighter to function correctly without mistaking it for a multiline comment.

### Root Cause
The problem occurs because the F# syntax highlighter in Prism.js identifies `(*...*)` as the beginning and end of a multi-line comment. However, the `(*)` operator used in a functional context should not trigger this comment parsing but is currently being misidentified due to the simplistic regex pattern for comment detection.


```javascript
### components/prism-fsharp.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
```
